note: A RockSim .rkt now opens on one of the simulations it stores, with each other motor set it stores as a flight configuration, where it used to open on the last simulation's motors, or, in a few files such as Loadstar.rkt, on a mix none of them flies: 571 of the 953 .rkt files the app is checked against now open with different motors. A design saved from an earlier import keeps what that import gave it, so open the original file again for any design you fly from a .rkt and check which simulation it opened. RockSim's plugged code is read as plugged, so a chute left on the ejection charge of a plugged motor no longer opens at burnout in the app - it does not open at all, as in the air. Recovery sizing at a pad above sea level, with a temperature typed and the pressure left blank, sized canopies for thicker air than the flight flies, so they came down faster than listed - 17.8 percent faster at the 2,682 m pad measured; with the pressure typed and the temperature blank they came down about 3 percent slower there. It also listed wrong rates with a chute slot empty, under a pinned stage mass and for a chute in a pod set, and on a recovery weight that left out the unburnt propellant of a motor whose ignition is set to Never, or miscounted the motors in a pod set or the pods on a booster. Parts a file places at an absolute station inside a pod, a catalogue-linked hollow nose and a zero-height camera shroud could each show more stability margin than the rocket has. An inner tube off the centreline, and any motor in it, now count their distance from the axis toward roll inertia in every model, so Classic Extended Barrowman no longer matches desktop OpenRocket 24.12 on that number, and no setting brings the old figure back; no design without canted fins flies differently for it. Three corrections: the v0.137 release renamed v0.136's What's New entry, which is now restored; v0.137 said an .rse exit it cannot believe is ignored with a note when no note was shown - there is one now; and the nozzle button still credited a manufacturer for an exit from your own .rse.
